title: Canonical system Hom, representative, limit and reduction reindexing maps
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; assume $\ell$ invertible on both schemes for finite coefficient-stage operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and their exact sectionwise inverse image $F$ [def-sf-adic-closed-reindexing-maps, def-weil-proetale-iso-sectionwise-inverse-image]. Use the actual strict system category and its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], the reindexing functor $F_\bullet$ and its pure-tensor-normalized tensor comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and the specified reduction/limit adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, closed evaluations and tensor comparisons [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

Define $c^0_{M,N}:FH_Y(M,N)\to H_X(FM,FN)$ at each finite coefficient level as the closed transpose of inverse canonical tensor comparison followed by $F(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})$. Define $c_{\bullet,A,B}:F_\bullet\mathcal I_Y(A,B)\to\mathcal I_X(F_\bullet A,F_\bullet B)$ by the identical closed-transpose construction on the actual system category. The recorded finite and system law interfaces refer to these same maps, with naturality, evaluation and transposition equations; they do not introduce a different chosen comparison.

For a ringed site, cochain complexes $K,I$, and K-injective $I$, use the actual sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], product-Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] and chosen derived internal Hom resolution [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Define its canonical K-injective representative isomorphism $e:R\mathcal Hom(QK,QI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,I)$ by the normalization $Q(a)\circ e=r$, in ordinary functional composition order, where $a:\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,I)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,J(I))$ is induced by the actual target-resolution augmentation and $r$ is the recorded resolution-factorization isomorphism. This normalization uniquely determines $e$.

Define the finite restriction/reindexing comparison by the inverse-image adjunction-unit formula on every local section, and derive that same ordinary isomorphism termwise. Define the ordinary limit comparison $\lim_X\circ F_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}F\circ\lim_Y$ as the unique isomorphism compatible with every actual limit projection through those restriction comparisons and the unit-normalized ordinary system evaluation comparison. Define $\lambda:\mathcal L_X\circ F_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}F\circ\mathcal L_Y$: it is the unique derived comparison satisfying the right-derived-functor unit square for every whole system complex and the induced finite projection equations. This normalization precedes finite evaluation and uses no equality detection by derived projections.

For every ambient completed-ring complex $M$, define $\rho_M:\mathcal R_X(FM)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\bullet\mathcal R_YM$ as the isomorphism of the actual adjunct of $F(\eta_{Y,M})$ followed by $\lambda^{-1}_{\mathcal R_YM}$. Its underlying map is defined before its invertibility and naturality law interface. All these are the already existing canonical maps with their uniqueness, augmentation, projection, resolution and law interfaces; no assertion of the downstream automorphism/Hom theorem is part of this definition.
